neighbours.label: dividing a quantity into a number of equal parts or chunks ("split n into m chunks", "the number of ... per"), strongest in code docstrings
fire:
def split_rows(rows, k):
    """Split rows into k batches."""
    size = len(rows) // k
    return size

def share(total, people):
    """Divide total into equal shares for people."""
    each = total // people
    return each

def partition(data, n):
    """Break data into n pieces of the same length."""
    step = len(data) // n
    return step

def pages(count, per_page):
    """Divide count records into pages."""
    num = count // per_page
    return num

def slices(seq, parts):
    """Cut seq into parts segments."""
    width = len(seq) // parts
    return width

def buckets(values, m):
    """Distribute values into m buckets."""
    per_bucket = len(values) // m
    return per_bucket

def tiles(area, tile):
    """How many tiles fit into area."""
    count = area // tile
    return count

def groups(students, g):
    """Split students into g teams."""
    team_size = len(students) // g
    return team_size
quiet:
def join_rows(rows, sep):
    """Join rows into one string."""
    text = sep.join(rows)
    return text

def greet(name, title):
    """Turn name into a greeting."""
    line = title + ' ' + name
    return line

def load(path, mode):
    """Read the file into memory."""
    data = open(path, mode).read()
    return data

def newest(items, key):
    """Sort items into newest-first order."""
    out = sorted(items, key=key)
    return out

def encode(text, table):
    """Translate text into codes."""
    codes = [table[c] for c in text]
    return codes

def log_in(user, password):
    """Log the user into the site."""
    ok = check(user, password)
    return ok

def insert(tree, node):
    """Put node into tree."""
    tree.add(node)
    return tree

def merge(left, right):
    """Merge two lists into one."""
    both = left + right
    return both

notes: Top examples are division/partition contexts in prose and code (fill the space without gaps, divide n to m chunks, number of, divided into blocks). Probes: code docstring 'Split items into k parts' 1.01; prose division sentences only 0.15-0.40, so the test uses code-shaped items. Near misses keep 'into' and the def/docstring shape without division.
